### Next bounded proof unit: actual routed hierarchy bodies

The completed ordered-factor theorem does not by itself cover the distinct routing generated for each operation by `src/frontend/sized/lower.rs::Graph::frame/route`. The next unit connects **actual current hierarchy bodies and exact complex coefficients** to a common ordered coordinate frame `(control, target A, target B, rest)`, applies the existing shared-control exchange theorem, and transports the result back through the actual routes.

Begin with small current consume/return source programs and preserve their actual emitted artifacts before changing any proof: a non-leading shared control, asymmetric target order, a disjoint untouched frame, and a wrong-inverse-route counterexample. These are executable translations of the intended local exchange, not adoption of future borrowed-call syntax.

Required theorem premises must remain explicit and tied to the same actual artifact/body: complete input/output interfaces and owner order from the relevant `NodeTyping.checkAll` conditions; actual wiring nodes and freshly checked summaries; a real bijection with two-sided inverse equations for the forward map and the computed inverse; and evaluations of the original provider/leaf definitions. `Wiring.valid` or a successful wiring inspection alone proves neither bijectivity nor an inverse. Different step routes may not simply be assumed identical. Retain zero-width owners and phase where the selected interfaces admit them.

The desired conclusion is equality of both actual evaluations' coefficients and their action on arbitrary external-reference amplitudes, without a separability assumption. Connect through existing executable `apply`/routing definitions and checked routing lemmas. A generic conjugation equality detached from the concrete body constructors is insufficient.

Validation requires building/auditing the actual definitions and theorem types, bounded positive and noncommuting/wrong-routing examples, independent review, and refreshing current source/proof bindings before integration. No new maximum-size cases, project axioms, unsafe definitions or admission record is introduced.

Source access contracts remain a separate prerequisite: ordered footprints, range/overlap checks, locality beyond control-sector preservation, lifetime/owner restoration, clean/dirty behavior and assignment semantics are not yet a complete adopted packet.
